chapter_theme: Natrinai 301 to 320: the end of the millet field and the guarded midnight in kurinji and neythal; the false rain and the lying promise of the man gone for wealth; a man melted from his journey by her silence; and the courtesan's voice, mocking a go-between and a town of anxious wives, and grieving as an old boat laid aside.

301.reading: The friend, to herself, recalls how the mother praises the girl item by item, a body like the fresh kurinji bloom of the long hill, rain-dark eyes like paired flowers of the spring, a peacock's grace, a parrot's speech, a doll's beauty, and sees that the girl the mother never once forgets is the one now kept from her lover.
301.nuance: The catalogue of beauty is the mother's, not the lover's, and that is the point: the same loving attention that praises every limb is the watch that never lapses, so the friend hears in the praise the reason the man is kept away.

colophon.thurai: சேட்படுத்து பிரிவின்கண் அன்பின் இயற்கையில் தகுவகையதோர் ஆற்றாமையினான் என்று தோழி தன்னுள்ளே சொல்லியது

thinai_evidence.note: the kurinji bloom of the long hill and the mountain spring

thurai_akam.speaker: thozhi
thurai_akam.note: the friend speaks to herself; the praise she repeats is the mother's

302.reading: The woman, seeing the season pass, says that though the forest has flowered with konrai clusters as lovely as jewelled women, surely the man who crossed the far waste, where elephant-kicked dust hides the old sad track among hard-cored velam trees, will notice the therul flowers strewn on the dark bushes that face the coming rain.
302.nuance: She does not doubt his love but his eyes: the rain's flowers are everywhere at home, and her hope is that somewhere on his road the same sign is falling where he must see it.

colophon.thurai: பருவம் கழிந்தது கண்டு தலைமகள் சொல்லியது

thinai_evidence.note: a wife waiting at home as the rains' flowers come, not the parting on the road

303.reading: The woman tells her friend that at deep midnight, when the bustling hamlet has fallen silent, every cry of the anril joined with its mate in the palmyra nest of the common ground keeps her sleepless and wasting, and she asks whether the lord of the shore, where the shark tears the fishermen's nets and roams the deep water, holds in his heart the thought that she suffers for him.
303.nuance: The paired anril is no comfort but a reproach, a creature that does not part from its mate crying beside her; the shark that tears the net and swims free may hint at a man who slips every bond, but no second correspondence is drawn, so it stays scene.

colophon.thurai: வேட்கை தாங்ககில்லாளாய்த் தோழிக்குத் தலைமகள் சொல்லியது சிறைப்புறத்தான் என்பது மலிந்ததூஉம் ஆம்

thinai_evidence.note: fishermen, the shark and the lord of the shore

304.reading: Answering her friend's reassurance, the woman says that the hill lord's cool fragrant-garlanded chest is like the hands of those who kill the asunam, full of pleasure and of pain: when he joins her, her beauty joins her, and when he parts, pallor fades her gem-and-gold complexion and wrecks her looks.
304.nuance: The asunam is the creature that is lured by music and then killed, so the simile says that his chest gives joy and pain from the same hand, not by turns from different causes; the parrots calling like a wind-blown horn set the scene of the hill.

colophon.thurai: வரையாது நெடுங்காலம் வந்தொழுக ஆற்றாளாகிய தலைமகள் வன்புறை எதிர் மொழிந்தது

thinai_evidence.note: millet, parrots and the hill lord

comparisons.tenor: his chest, which gives both joy and pain

305.reading: The mother tells the friend that the striped ball, the withered vayalai creeper, the nochchi with clusters like a peacock's foot and the garden her daughter used to see alone have become a burning pain to her; and she wonders whether the girl, hearing a striped dove's lonely call on a leafless branch in the shimmering heat, fears that the hill pass may harm the young man with the white spear.
305.nuance: The mother's grief turns at line 6 into the daughter's fear: she pictures the girl on the road not afraid for herself but for the man she went with.

colophon.thurai: நற்றாய் தோழிக்குச் சொல்லியது மனை மருட்சியும் ஆம்

thinai_evidence.note: a leafless branch, the heat and the hard pass

thurai_akam.speaker: nartaay
thurai_akam.note: the mother bewildered in the house, speaking to no one named

306.reading: Within hearing of the man, the friend says the millet the father sowed is being reaped, the hunters sending the cold-handed hill girl home with kind words, and the stubble stands like a festival ground after the feast; how will he come, day after day, to see the sad bare field where the sweet-voiced girl once stayed?
306.nuance: The friend says nothing of marriage; the empty field does the work, since its emptiness means she is now kept at home and he can meet her only by asking for her.

colophon.thurai: புனம் மடிவு உரைத்துச் செறிப்பு அறிவுறீஇயது சிறைப்புறமும் ஆம்

thinai_evidence.note: the millet field, the hunters and the hill girl

307.reading: The friend tells the woman, anxious that the tryst is delayed, that the lord of the long sands is coming, his chariot bells ringing and his young men calling; let them hide behind the dark trunk of the drum-rooted punnai and, when he comes at midnight to the flowered grove, watch a little of the pain he suffers at not finding them.
307.nuance: The comfort is a game: by turning the waiting round, so that he is the one who searches and grieves, the friend gives the woman back the upper hand the delay had taken from her.

colophon.thurai: குறி நீட ஆற்றாளாகிய தலைமகளைத் தோழி வற்புறுத்தியது

thinai_evidence.note: the punnai of the shore grove and the lord of the sands

occasion.words: குறி நீட ஆற்றாளாகிய தலைமகளைத் தோழி வற்புறுத்தியது

308.reading: The man, urged by his heart to go for wealth, tells it that when she noticed the bustle of departure she came slowly, tears in her flower-like eyes, unable to ask or to stop him, troubled like a doll whose mechanism has broken, and pressed herself to his chest; and at that his wealth-filled heart melted into hers like a fresh pot of wet clay set out in the heavy rain, and he will not go.
308.nuance: She wins without a word: the poem stresses that she could neither question nor hold him, and the silence is what undoes his resolve; the unfired pot in the rain says his purpose dissolved, not that it was overruled.

colophon.thurai: நெஞ்சினால் பொருள் வலிக்கப்பட்ட தலைமகன் தலைமகளை எய்தி ஆற்றானாய் நெஞ்சினைச் சொல்லிச் செலவு அழுங்கியது

thinai_evidence.note: a parting for wealth, here given up

comparisons.vehicle: ஈர் மண் செய்கை நீர் படு பசுங் கலம் பெரு மழைப் பெயற்கு ஏற்றாங்கு
comparisons.tenor: his wealth-filled heart melting into hers

occasion.words: நெஞ்சினால் பொருள் வலிக்கப்பட்ட தலைமகன் தலைமகளை எய்தி ஆற்றானாய் நெஞ்சினைச் சொல்லிச் செலவு அழுங்கியது

309.reading: The woman consoles her friend, who sees her slack arms, faded lines and lost leaf-bright colour and grieves that she caused it: do not sink in grief; you may say that no one knows the hill lord's friendship has become our trouble, but I trust his friendship.
309.nuance: The roles are reversed from the usual: the friend has broken down and the heroine does the comforting, and her comfort is a single act of trust set against all the visible evidence of her own wasting.

colophon.thurai: வரைவு நீட ஆற்றாள் எனக் கவன்று தான் ஆற்றாளாகிய தோழியைத் தலைமகள் ஆற்றுவித்தது

thinai_evidence.note: the banana of the great hill and the hill lord

310.reading: The woman tells the singing-woman who has come as the man's go-between that the town's lord, where lotuses burn like lamps among leaves like elephant ears and the vaalai leaps in the deep water so the bathing women flee, has agreed to a bride tomorrow, and that her clever words are a cover with nothing inside, like the loud drum in the hand of a bard who is fed on gifts of elephants.
310.nuance: Lines 5 to 8 are hard to construe (who has agreed to give a daughter, and who are the mothers with failing speech), so the exact charge is uncertain; the leaping fish that scatters the bathing women may glance at the man's disorder in the households, but only one correspondence can be drawn, so it stays scene.

colophon.thurai: விறலியை எதிர்ப்பட்ட பரத்தை சொல்லியதூஉம் ஆம்

thinai_evidence.note: lotus pond, the vaalai and the bathing ford of the fields

thurai_akam.speaker: thozhi
thurai_akam.note: from line 12 of the text, which is a colophon line (வாயிலாகப் புக்க விறலியைத் தோழி சொல்லியது) run into the verse

311.reading: Consoling the woman who suffers from gossip, the friend praises their old town, rich with paddy when it rains and with white salt from the backwater pans when it is dry, and its ford sweet with the smoke of roasting fish and njazhal flowers; its grove has one fault only, that the bees drunk on punnai pollen hum so loudly that his chariot's sweet sound is hard to hear.
311.nuance: The friend never names the gossip; she moves the blame onto the grove, where the drunken bees' din drowns his chariot, and the hearer is left to match the bees with the talking town.

colophon.thurai: அலர் கூறப்பட்டு ஆற்றாளாகிய தலைமகளைத் தோழி ஆற்றுவித்தது

thinai_evidence.note: salt pans, the backwater and the shore trees

occasion.words: அலர் கூறப்பட்டு ஆற்றாளாகிய தலைமகளைத் தோழி ஆற்றுவித்தது

ullurai.tenor: the gossiping town and the man's kept-off visits

pairs.situation: the town's loud talk about the lovers

pairs.scene: நெடுந் தேர் இன் ஒலி கேட்டலோ அரிதே
pairs.situation: the gossip keeps him from coming openly

ullurai.speaker_fit: the friend uses the bees of the shore punnai, a thing of the neythal poem's own grove (porul 7.27)

312.reading: The man, set on wealth, tells his heart that he grieves and it grieves too: in the misty cold when the rains have stopped, when the shivering white heron sits with folded wings and even the decoy hunter takes up his stakes in pity, she who shivers in the summer months even with him beside her, what will become of her in the north wind's great cold?
312.nuance: The reason to go is never stated, only the reason not to; the hunter who lays off in pity of a cold bird is the one figure in the scene who does what the man is being asked to do.

colophon.thurai: பொருள் வலித்த தலைமகன் நெஞ்சினை நெருங்கிச் சொல்லியது

thinai_evidence.note: a man weighing a parting for wealth

occasion.words: பொருள் வலித்த தலைமகன் நெஞ்சினை நெருங்கிச் சொல்லியது

iraicchi.act: the decoy hunter, in pity of the shivering heron, takes up his stakes and lets it be
iraicchi.sense: even a hunter spares a creature shivering in the cold, so the man should not leave his shivering wife in it

313.reading: With the man listening, the friend asks the woman what will become of them, now that he who, longing to see her, dressed her thick hair with fresh vengai blossom like a goldsmith's work must find the koothalam grove on the kaanthal slope deserted; for the millet they guard with shouts, its leaves dried, has reached the time for reaping, and they will go back to town.
313.nuance: The vengai flowers he set in her hair are the memory of the kalavu, and the reaping is its end; the friend speaks as one who fears the separation, so that the listening man hears the date of it.

colophon.thurai: தோழி சிறைப்புறமாகத் தலைமகட்குச் சொல்லுவாளாய் புனம் அழிவு உரைத்துசெறிப்பு அறிவுறீஇயது

thinai_evidence.note: vengai, kaanthal and the millet field

comparisons.tenor: the unceasing shouting over the millet

314.reading: The wasting woman says that the old never get back their lost youth and no one knows the measure of a life, yet the men who held her close, saying 'let the night pass so', lied by the strength of their words and went, may they live, into the long hot track where a dull lonely dove climbs the swaying kalli, whose pods crack like snapping fingers, and calls to its fallen mate.
314.nuance: The opening maxim is her argument against his journey: youth does not return and life's length is unknown, so the time he spends earning is spent out of the only time love has; her blessing on the liars is bitter.

colophon.thurai: பிரிவிடை மெலிந்த தலைமகள் சொல்லியது

thinai_evidence.note: the long track in the hot season, with kalli

comparisons.tenor: the cracking pods of the kalli

iraicchi.act: the lonely dove on the waste calls to its mate
iraicchi.sense: even a dove in the hot waste calls for its mate, while the man who went that way has left his own

315.reading: The courtesan, hurt, tells the lord of the ford, where an old boat with a broken prow, worn by years of beating surf, its work done, lies tied to the drum-like root of the punnai in the njazhal's shade and no longer gets its fragrant smoke, as ploughmen leave a spent ox in a grassy grove, that if he does not see the fault of so lightly dropping a bond so fully taken, all who love him will end like her, arms slack, eyes weeping, like burnt flowers.
315.nuance: Lines 1, 4 and 5 are hard to construe, so the reading of the worship (the boat once given incense, now not) and of the ox is uncertain.

colophon.thurai: தலைமகனைப் பரத்தை நொந்து சொல்லியது

thinai_evidence.note: the surf, the fishing boat and the shore trees

comparisons.vehicle: நல் எருது நடை வளம் வைத்தென உழவர் புல்லுடைக் காவில் தொழில் விட்டாங்கு
comparisons.tenor: the fishers leaving the old boat idle

ullurai.tenor: the courtesan, used and laid aside by the man

pairs.scene: மூத்து வினை போகிய முரி வாய் அம்பி
pairs.situation: the woman whose service to him is spent
she is no longer honoured or tended
she is kept tied, idle, at the edge of his life

ullurai.speaker_fit: the courtesan is not of the household and may use any thing freely (porul 7.29); the boat is of the shore she names

316.reading: The friend tells the wasting woman how foolish the sapphire cloud is: he left, stroking her brow, which he thought the moon of the wide sky, saying he would come when the mouval flowers show a beauty like her teeth, and before his wish is won and he returns, the cool rain cloud has poured down, hiding the rock ridges, and thundered across the wide sky.
316.nuance: Calling the cloud foolish declares the rain false: it has come before its time, so his promise is not yet broken; the comfort works by blaming the season rather than the man.

colophon.thurai: பிரிவிடை மெலிந்த தலைமகளைத் தோழி வற்புறுத்தது

thinai_evidence.note: the rain cloud, the cool rains and the mouval

317.reading: The friend asks the lord of the high hills, where the long millet ear curves like the raised trunk of a spotted tusker mated with his cow and the coral-beaked parrot carries it off, what will become of the girl's eyes, like the dark kuvalai she picked with her companions after bathing in the spring of her father's slope, if her mother learns of their love.
317.nuance: The parrot stealing the father's ripe millet suggests the man taking what the family guards, but only that one correspondence is drawn, so it stays scene; the threat is in the eyes, which will weep.

colophon.thurai: தோழி தலைமகனை வரைவு கடாயது

thinai_evidence.note: millet, parrot, hill and spring kuvalai

318.reading: The friend, told he is leaving, asks the man whether he even remembers the day they sat in the dappled shade of the omai, when a tall-tusked elephant came near without frightening them, broke branches and ate, then curled its trunk and went off by another path, and at once the young cow-elephant, sensing it, cried out alone till the hot rock clefts rang.
318.nuance: The friend tells only what the elephants did and leaves him to match it: he is the tusker who turns off by another path, and the cow's cry echoing in the rocks is what his leaving will bring.

colophon.thurai: பிரிவு உணர்த்தப்பட்ட தலைமகனைத் தோழி சொல்லியது

thinai_evidence.note: a parting, set among omai and the hot clefts

ullurai.tenor: the man about to leave and the woman left behind

pairs.situation: he turns away on another road, for wealth

pairs.scene: புன் தலை மடப் பிடி புலம்பிய குரலே
pairs.situation: she will grieve alone when he goes
his coming had once been gentle and near

ullurai.speaker_fit: the friend uses an elephant pair of the poem's own dry hill country (porul 7.27)

319.reading: The man, kept away by the close watch, says to himself that the tide has stopped roaring and the wind is still over the pollen-strewn grove, the male owl and its mate hoot fearfully from the crossroads of the sandy old town, and at midnight, when spirits walk in the thick dark and even the fish's eyes sleep, he lies awake longing to embrace the girl of doll-like beauty; what will become of him?
319.nuance: Everything in the night is stilled or asleep, even the fish that never closes its eyes, so his wakefulness is set against the whole world; the owl pair and the walking spirits make the hour that a meeting would need, and that the watch denies him.

colophon.thurai: காப்பு மிகுதிக்கண் ஆற்றானாகிய தலைமகன் தலைமகளை நினைந்து தன்னுள்ளே சொல்லியது

thinai_evidence.note: the tide, the shore grove and the sandy town

320.reading: The courtesan, within hearing of those on her side, says the festival is over and the drum is hung up, and if you ask what she meant: for no more than a young girl in a leaf skirt walking down the street, the town broke into uproar like the land of his enemies when Kaari entered the great street where old Ori was killed, and the fair-bangled wives shut the watch tight and grew anxious, guarding their husbands.
320.nuance: She mocks the wives by measuring their panic against a town sacked in war: one girl walking past is enough to make the household behave like a captured city.

colophon.thurai: பரத்தை தனக்குப் பாங்காயினார் கேட்ப நெருங்கிச் சொல்லியது

thinai_evidence.note: wives guarding husbands against a courtesan after the festival

comparisons.vehicle: ஓரிக் கொன்ற ஒரு பெருந் தெருவில் காரி புக்க நேரார் புலம்
comparisons.tenor: the uproar of the town at the girl's passing

thurai_akam.speaker: parathai

occasion.words: பரத்தை தனக்குப் பாங்காயினார் கேட்ப நெருங்கிச் சொல்லியது

thurai_akam.note: spoken to her own companions, aimed at the wife's household

links.note: Both set a sleepless woman against a night in which everyone else sleeps: Kural 1168 says the night that lulls all creatures has only her for company; in Natrinai 303 the hamlet has fallen silent and only the paired anril cries.
links.teaches: The couplet's lonely vigil turns out, in the Natrinai scene, to have one other waker, a bird that has its mate, so her sleeplessness is measured against a pairing she lacks, and her question is whether he lies awake too.

links.note: Both make pallor the immediate price of the lover's absence: Kural 1187 says it came the moment she turned in his embrace; Natrinai 304 says beauty joins her when he joins and pallor wrecks it when he parts.
links.teaches: The couplet records the speed of the pallor; the Natrinai woman draws the moral that the same chest is joy and harm at once, like the hand that plays to the asunam and then kills it.

links.note: Both are the friend's warning, heard by the man, that the millet field is ending and the girl will be confined: in 313 the crop has just reached reaping time; in 306 the reaping is done and the field is bare stubble.
links.teaches: Read together they show the harvest working as a clock for the secret love, with the friend's message moving from 'soon' to 'now' as the millet goes from ripe ear to stubble.

links.note: Both describe the reaped millet field as a broken stalk-head stubble in nearly the same words (பொறை இறுத்த கோல் தலை இருவி; குலவுப்பொறை யிறுத்த கோல்தலை மருவி), and both picture the man finding it empty and sad (பைதல்; பைதலன்).
links.teaches: The shared formula shows that the reaped field was a fixed sign of the closed meeting-place: Natrinai's friend uses it as a threat to make him ask for the girl, while Akananuru's friend imagines him already standing there grieving.

links.note: Both are the moment the man announces departure: in Kural 1151 she answers with a sharp demand, tell me if you are not going; in Natrinai 308 she can neither ask nor stop him and only presses against his chest.
links.teaches: The Kural gives the woman a defiant sentence to stop the journey, while Natrinai shows wordless grief doing what the sentence could not, since it is her silence that melts his resolve.

links.note: Both start from the same premise, that youth passes and does not return; Naladiyar 11 concludes that the wise renounce desire from childhood; Natrinai 314 uses it to condemn the man who left an embrace for wealth.
links.teaches: The same commonplace of fleeting youth served opposite ends: for the akam woman it is a reason to spend youth in love now, for the didactic poet a reason to give love up, so the ascetic use of the maxim takes over an argument love poetry had already made.

links.note: Both argue from an unknown lifespan against putting something off: Naladiyar 19 says do not defer good deeds because the wind may drop the unripe fruit; Natrinai 314 says no one knows the measure of a life, yet he left her for later gain.
links.teaches: The pairing shows that 'do not defer, life is short' was a shared argument whose object changed with the genre, virtue in the Naladiyar and love in the Natrinai, where wealth-seeking is the deferral blamed.

links.note: Both are the friend's comfort that the rain is false: in Kuruntokai 66 the konrai is foolish for taking stray rain for the season 'before the season comes' (பருவம் வாரா அளவை); in Natrinai 316 the cloud itself is foolish for pouring 'before he comes' (வரல் வாரா அளவை).
links.teaches: Natrinai moves the foolishness from the flowers that believe the rain to the cloud that sends it, so the consolation could discredit the season at either end, the sign or its source.

links.note: Both are the same midnight on the guarded shore: in 303 the woman lies awake while the hamlet sleeps and asks whether he knows; in 319 the man, kept away by the watch, lies awake while even the fish sleep.
links.teaches: Set side by side, 319 answers the question in 303: he is awake too, and the anthology places the same sleepless midnight on both sides of the guard that separates them.

links.note: Purananuru 158 lists Ori of Kolli and Malaiyan who rode Kaari side by side among the seven great givers; Natrinai 320 remembers the street where Ori was killed and Kaari entered as a byword for a stricken town.
links.teaches: The bards' canon of seven generous patrons hides that two of them were enemies, one killing the other, and the love poem shows that killing had become a proverb for a town in panic.

source_issues: 310: line 12 (வாயிலாகப் புக்க விறலியைத் தோழி சொல்லியது) is a colophon line run into the verse; the colophon thurai ends 'சொல்லியதூஉம் ஆம்', the alternative to it. The verse has 11 lines.
316: the colophon thurai has வற்புறுத்தது, a misprint for வற்புறுத்தியது; copied as it stands.
305: line 7 carries a repaired TSCII form (தெள் விளி); 311: line 2 ஃ restored from the old encoding; 317: line 1 -ஒடு vowel sign restored (text flags).

313: line 3 (கண்ணழி கட்டழித்து) is obscure; 310: lines 5 to 8 are hard to construe; 315: lines 1, 4 and 5 are hard to construe; 312: line 4 (காழ் களைந்தருள) is uncertain; 301: line 9 (தேம் மறப்பு அறியா) is uncertain.
302: the colophon thinai is பாலை; the poem is the wife at home reading the season's flowers, and I infer mullai (irutthal), with the road's paalai things marked as mixed.
Natrinai colophons rarely name the addressee; addressees marked as inferred are mine.
